Ahh, you are proposing to use Redfish over the Host Interface for the BIOS to find the pending BIOS configuration setting changes, and to find the information needed to expose the host interfaec in SMBIOIS.

The Redfish permissions are not designed, specified or modeled for this. While it can be done through OEM additions, this is also not the reasoning to have the bootstrap account.  The DMTF expects the BIOS to use other unspecified communication channel(s) to the BMC (including PLDM).  (There are older posts in the forum mentioning this in the discussion of permissions and readonly/readwrite objects).

This doesn't mean it can't be done.  But it probably wants to be an account with an OEM role, and have a different lifetime such as only valid while the host is in the BIOS (or some phase of BIOS).

It's not required for the BIOS to acquire credentials, it's equally valid for only the host os to acquire them.   In this case it'd be expected but not required for the BIOS to add the smbios records to describe how to locate the service.


Oh, you are describing your proposal to use the Redfish interface and Bootstrap account by the BIOS using the HostInterface, not the interface itself.

How would the administrator inform the BIOS that it wishes to have the account availbe to UEFI or HostOS?   Disabling it precludes the usage at a later stage.  Enablinig it likewise exposes a security sensive interface that could (with your model) consume the settings meant for the next boot causing a loss of control in addition to the direct acccess to the manager from an untrusted environment.

which properties did you anticipate?   disable bootstrap account until the next boot copies it from enable after reset?   

this is why I propose storing the role, the bootstrap credential enable, enable after reset, and accounts together in hif and just communicating the account and password back to ipmid (but not sending the password over dbus directly.  Maybe via a fd, but if it goes to the host interface over the standard protocols this security precaution may be mute)

So far it has little focus on the Redfish Host Interface object.   The original proposal focused on how BIOS would use a Bootstrap account enabled by the interface to discover information to advertise in SMBIOS, and the pending changes Redfish has recorded for the BIOS.   Additional discussions have explored more how the Bootstrap accounts would be managed.  

As stated below
- There is additional information needed to implement the Redfish HostInterface object, 
- I believe the Bootstrap account design needs more focus. (I'm ok with a separate section in this design but would also accept splitting it into its own design)
- I suggest caution about using a bootstrap account and Redfish to obtain and process the information proposed.

The host Interface specification describes how firmware will expose the designated interface, and a mechanism to obtain credentials to obtain access to the manager authorized by being software started on the machine (Bootstrap Account).
This last sentence is a restatement  of the  Problem Definition, and not related to the Bios Settings manager.
supporting communication from the BMC just requires IP reachability.
the easy integration is the BootStrap account on the interface advertised by the firmware and the credentiails that can be provisioned to it.
As DSP0270 indicates, the account is created to initiate communication, anticipating using it to provision an account to be used with persistence.
Are there more details about what the host-if-daemon does? It seems like maybe its work could just be done by the user manager and maybe the phosphor settings manager.

There is a need for some service to actively respond to host state transitions and copy the `EnableAfterReset` attribute to the `CurrentlyEnabled` attribute.  If this is the only change its reasonable to implement this within the user-manager repository.

however, I hesitate hosting this in the existing user-manager daemon.  I believe (without any code review) that the repository only exposes existing state and exposes methods to add/update objects it manages - users for `passwd` entries.  But probably additional state for LDAP configuration.  But this is adding additional state and management and initiating changes on system events a much more active role and business logic.
 
If we support disabling the network by patching the interface Disable or creating isolated networks, there are service targets to stop or start.  The USB network gadget might need to be reset each host boot.  Implementing these additional objects may suggest a separate daemon.

Why would one want to enable IPMI over LAN on the host Interface?  Why would this ever be a feature as opossed to ipmi over the host interface? just to obtain the Manager side off the LAN IPv4 parameters?  Is there any high bandwidth IPMI usage (Ok, I'm aware some have added blob transport to send firmware and logs).

This looks like squeezing a round peg into a square hole.  The Obvious reason was to find a "standard" interface that already had some of the information.  But the next two items show it's not enough (although they are advertised with service discovery protocol).
You are missing the certificate fingerprint bit. The BIOS needs to be able to get the bmcweb certificate fingerprint to be able to trust it over TLS once it is using the redfish host interface.
Thats not in the specification.  The DNS hostname optionally included but there is no way to establish DNS security.   Perhaps this should be raised to the DMTF (by a member wanting the interface).

DMTF created a whole DSP to standardize exporting BIOS configuration parameters over PLDM.  Clearly they expect this to be used for standard settings.

Secure boot enable could be a setting described by a schema, but I agree even the secure boot DB seems beyond the settings interface.  I expect these could be expose as generic effectors today, or transported through other state.

They have now exposed a file object and directory concept; these EFI variables could be exposed as file objects or an additioal custom interface.
